source.title: Two Open Problems for Absolutely Convergent Dirichlet Series

accepted.question_text: Let Λ=(λ_n)_{n≥0} be a strictly increasing sequence of nonnegative numbers with λ_0=0, let F(z)=∑_{n=0}^{∞} a_n e^{zλ_n}, let M(x,F)=sup_t |F(x+it)|, and let μ(x,F)=max_n |a_n|e^{xλ_n}. For ψ in L, let S_ψ(Λ) be the class of entire Dirichlet series with infinitely many nonzero coefficients satisfying |a_n|≤e^{-λ_nψ(λ_n)} for all sufficiently large n. Assume h∈L_0 and that conditions (4) and (5) of the paper hold, so that for every F∈S_ψ(Λ) there exist c>0 and x_0 such that M(x,F)<μ(x,F) h(cx) for all x≥x_0. What is the exact, i.e. sharp, value of the constant c for which this inequality can always be guaranteed?
accepted.context_brief: Sharp constant in the S_ψ(Λ) growth bound

evidence.quote: For ψ∈ L let Sψ(Λ) denote the class of entire Dirichlet series (1) (i.e. F∈ S(Λ) def = S+∞(Λ)) such that ♯{n: an̸= 0} = +∞ and |an|≤ exp{−λnψ(λn)} (n≥ n0).
conditions (4), (5) (∀F∈ Sψ(Λ))(∃c > 0)(∃x0)(∀x≥ x0): M(x, F) < µ(x, F)h(cx).
Question 1. What is the exact value of the constant c in the previous inequality?

accepted.question_text: Let S^0(Λ) denote the class of Dirichlet series absolutely convergent in the half-plane {z∈ℂ: Re z<0}. Develop for S^0(Λ) an analogue of Theorem A or Proposition 1 from the paper. Concretely, determine hypotheses under which one can prove for F∈S^0(Λ) a no-exceptional-set upper estimate of the same kind as the S_ψ(Λ) estimates in Theorem A or Proposition 1, namely bounds comparing M(x,F)=sup_t |F(x+it)| to the maximal term μ(x,F)=max_n |a_n|e^{xλ_n} through expressions such as μ(x,F)h(ln μ(x,F)) or the stronger Proposition 1 type bound μ(x,F)h(xd(x)).
accepted.context_brief: Analogue of Theorem A or Proposition 1 for S^0(Λ)

evidence.quote: Let Λ = ( λn)∞ n=0 be a sequence of nonnegative numbers such that 0 = λ0 < λ n < λ n+1 ... and Sa(Λ) be the class of absolutely convergent in the complex half-plane Πa ={z = σ + it∈ C: σ < a, t∈ R}, ... Dirichlet series of the form F (z) = ∑ an e^{zλn}.
Theorem A ([1]). Let ψ∈ L ... Then (∀F∈ Sψ(Λ))(∃x0)(∀x≥ x0): M(x, F) < µ(x, F)h(ln µ(x, F)) holds if and only if ...
Proposition 1. If ψ∈ L, h ∈ L0 and conditions(4), (5) hold, then (∀d∈ L0)(∀F∈ Sψ(Λ))(∃x0)(∀x≥ x0): M(x, F) < µ(x, F)h(xd(x)).
Problem 1. Set an analogue of Theorem A or Proposition 1 for the class S0(Λ).

accepted.question_text: Let ψ∈L_1, let S^0_ψ(Λ) be the class of Dirichlet series F∈S^0(Λ) such that |a_n|≤e^{λ_n/ψ(λ_n)} for all sufficiently large n, and let M(x,F)=sup_t |F(x+it)| and μ(x,F)=max_n |a_n|e^{xλ_n}. Assume h∈L_0 and that conditions (7) and (5) of the paper hold, so that for every F∈S^0_ψ(Λ) there exist c>0 and x_0<0 with M(x,F)<μ(x,F) h(c/|x|) for all x∈[x_0,0). What is the exact, i.e. sharp, value of the constant c for which this inequality can always be guaranteed?
accepted.context_brief: Sharp constant in the S^0_ψ(Λ) half-plane bound

evidence.quote: For ψ∈ L1 let S0 ψ(Λ) denote the class of Dirichlet series F∈ S0(Λ) such that |an|≤ exp{ λn / ψ(λn) }, n ≥ n0.
Corollary 1. If ψ∈ L1, h ∈ L0 and conditions(7), (5) hold, then (∀F∈ S0 ψ(Λ))(∃c > 0)(∃x0 < 0)(∀x∈ [x0, 0)): M(x, F) < µ(x, F)h(c/|x|).
Question 2. What is the exact value of constant c in the previous inequality?
